title: Kanpur flour, dal & grain mills: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Kanpur flour or dal mill buys wheat or pulses, cleans and grinds them, and sells atta, maida, sooji or dal into wholesale and retail. **Cash is made on throughput and turnover, not on price** — a CARA-rated roller flour and dal mill ran a PBLIDT margin of 1.20% and PAT margin of 0.35% in FY19 [10]. So when a proposal lands, check the margin line first; if the borrower quotes double-digit EBITDA, ask for the audited P&L and GST returns to reconcile. ## Where value and cash sit
Value sits in the brand and the distribution reach, not the machine. AWL Agri's branded and functional lines carry far higher margin than staples, but need spend on brand building and consumer connect [4][5]. **Working capital is the real loan here** — grain must be bought at harvest and held. Kanpur grain prices are rising on tight supply [3], so when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower is funding inventory with our limit or with supplier credit; if stock days are stretching while prices rise, ask for the purchase and sales register month by month. ## What has changed now
Two local facts matter. UP rice millers are protesting the discontinuation of incentive payments [1], so treat any Kanpur rice-milling exposure as incentive-dependent revenue that may not repeat. Separately, the state is moving on closed BIC mill land for new industry [2] — that is a land story, not a lending story yet. **The data call is Caution (63)** [D]; UP GST is running 14.2% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], which supports trade volumes, but bank credit is growing 25.3% YoY against output of 5.1% [D], so the system is lending ahead of production. ## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
Pursue branded atta and dal millers with own distribution, and second-generation mills with steady offtake. Avoid pure rice millers leaning on state incentives [1] and unbranded grinders selling on price alone [10]. **Structure against the cycle**: cash credit sized to stock and book debts, monthly stock and receivable statements, and a covenant that drawing power is recalculated each month. Take GST returns, e-way bills and godown stock statements every month. Peer rating reports show strong liquidity where credit utilisation stays low — 27% average utilisation with Rs. 79.0 crore cash [8], and 20% in FY2025 falling to 12% in 9M FY2026 [9]; use utilisation as your comfort test. ## Early-warning signs
- **Incentive or subsidy receivable ageing** — if a rice miller's receivable from the state crosses one quarter, stop enhancement and ask for the sanction letter. - **Margin compression** — a PAT margin drifting toward the 0.35% seen in FY19 [10] means the borrower is buying volume with price; cut limit. - **Raw material price spike** [3] with flat sales — inventory is being held, not sold; ask for godown verification.
watch: Monthly GST returns and e-way bills
Filing gap or falling e-way volume -> freeze enhancement, inspect godown
Stock days rising while sales flat -> reprice drawing power, seek collateral
Quarterly incentive receivable from UP government
Ageing beyond one quarter -> stop fresh disbursal, ask for sanction order
